audit.report: A replayable inventory reconciliation batch job blocked checkout by holding an idle open transaction for 4.1 seconds, causing 12 sessions to wait on locks. Checkout success fell to 52% over 15 seconds with 29 timeouts, then to 26% over 30 seconds with 89 of 120 failures, risking about $13,647 per minute against an $18,400 per minute run-rate. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, and the Continuity Guardian accepted because the job is replayable, idempotent, checkpoint-resumable, and interruptible, with no protected settlements or change-calendar conflicts. The authority authorized the action in one round, and the executor terminated pid 109293. Verification confirmed recovery: no lock waits remain and checkout succeeded 36 of 36 times over 10 seconds at 100%, above the 95% SLO.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 109293) was idle in an open transaction and held locks that blocked checkout sessions.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, monitor open-transaction duration and lock waits on checkout tables so a blocker is detected before success drops below the 95% SLO.

Pre-authorize termination of replayable, idempotent, checkpoint-resumable batch jobs like inventory_reconcile during checkout degradation to avoid waiting through the 60-second business tolerance window.
audit.negotiation_critique: The guardians reached agreement in one round with no wasted proposals; both cited the same observed evidence and no invariant overrode the decision.
follow_ups: Review why batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile) stayed idle in transaction for 4.1 seconds and add an alert for open transactions exceeding a few seconds.
Confirm the terminated job resumed from its last checkpoint and completed its 4-minute replay without re-blocking checkout.

proposal.rationale: Checkout is timing out: 12 sessions waiting on locks, root blocker pid 109293 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session; last statement SELECT 1 [DB-1]. Checkout success is 52% over last 15s with 29 timeouts [TEL-1], and business impact shows 71% success vs 95% SLO with $5,412/min at risk [BIZ-1]. The blocker holds locks while idle, so terminating it releases locks and unblocks checkout sessions. I need registry, calendar, settlements, and tradeoff evidence before finalizing to confirm replayability, interrupt policy, protected settlements, and cost of waiting vs interrupting.
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating pid 109293 releases its locks, allowing the 1 blocked session and the 12 waiting checkout sessions to proceed; checkout success should recover toward SLO and revenue at risk should decline.
proposal.risk_assessment: The batch_worker transaction may be mid-work; termination could interrupt replayable inventory work. Need to confirm replayability/interrupt policy from registry and that no protected settlements are in flight before executing.
